children: Retail sales in the Netherlands rose by 2.8% year-on-year in July 2026, marking the softest growth since February and easing from a 2.9% increase in the previous month.
Food and beverage retailers posted 1.5% revenue growth, down from 2.3% in June as smaller gains in supermarkets (1.6% vs 2.6%) more than offset an improvement at specialty stores (0.7% vs 0.4%).
Online revenues also rose at a lesser extent (3.8% vs 7.5%), with all major online retailers recording slower sales growth than a year ago.

Meanwhile, turnover in the non-food sector increased further (3.6% vs 3.3%), led by drugstores (12.5% vs 7.4%) and consumer electronics and white goods (5.5% vs 5.8%), while furniture and home furnishings (2.6% vs -0.8%) and shoes and leather goods (0.6% vs -4.7%) also rebounded.
On a seasonally adjusted monthly basis, retail activity grew by 0.6% in July, recovering from a 0.1% fall in the preceding period.

title: Dutch Retail Sales Growth at 5-Month Low
